body.x: [Las Vegas, USA = AVING News] SPAID drew strong attention from global public-sector and urban infrastructure stakeholders at CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition held in Las Vegas, as it unveiled its 3D GIS platform strategy integrating disaster response and geospatial intelligence for smart city safety infrastructure.

At CES 2026, SPAID presented a MAP-based platform architecture focused on climate disaster response, including wildfires and floods, enabling real-time interpretation and visualization of geospatial data. Rather than showcasing isolated technologies, the company emphasized clearly defined product categories tailored to specific disaster types and operational use cases.
"Wildfire and Flood Response ‘Geo Safe MAP’… From Spread Prediction to Route Recommendations"

SPAID defines its wildfire response solution under the category ‘Geo Safe MAP.’ The platform integrates and analyzes diverse geospatial and environmental data—such as terrain slope, vegetation type, and wind direction—within a 3D spatial environment, based on the ignition point of a wildfire. Using this analysis, the system predicts fire spread patterns and recommends optimal response routes, moving beyond traditional manual-based firefighting access paths to routes optimized for real-world conditions.

While conventional disaster response systems rely primarily on maps and numerical data, Geo Safe MAP is designed to enable decision-makers to understand disaster situations as spatial environments. Through 3D simulations that accurately reflect on-site terrain, the platform supports intuitive risk assessment and strategic response planning.

Flood and inundation response capabilities are implemented by linking water level gauges and sensor data to visualize the inflow and spread of water across affected areas over time. Beyond simply marking flooded zones, the system allows real-time monitoring of where water enters and how it propagates through urban and natural landscapes in a 3D space.

This approach supports proactive response measures, including early control and evacuation planning for flood-prone areas, supplementing existing systems that typically enable disaster recognition only two to three hours in advance. SPAID expects the technology to help overcome the limitations of post-incident-focused disaster management frameworks.
"Geospatial Intelligence ‘Geo Data MAP’… A Collaboration Model for Data Owners"

Beyond disaster response, SPAID also introduced its ‘Geo Data MAP’ platform, which focuses on geospatial data integration itself. Geo Data MAP is a 3D GIS platform that consolidates drone imagery, satellite data, and existing GIS datasets, providing a foundation for organizations that possess geospatial data but lack the infrastructure to operationalize it.

At CES 2026, SPAID discussed a collaboration model with a GIS-specialized company based in Abu Dhabi, exploring ways to integrate the partner’s geospatial datasets into SPAID’s platform. This case highlights SPAID’s potential expansion from a solution provider to a global geospatial platform operator.

Meanwhile, SPAID has already secured proven deployment experience in Korea. The smart city safety and security system project for the Solaseado Smart City in Haenam County, Jeollanam-do Province, has been officially awarded and is currently underway, serving as a representative example of SPAID’s technology being applied to real urban infrastructure. At CES 2026, this ongoing project also served as a reference point for further discussions with local governments and public-sector organizations.
